source_row.rationale: An AIIR is maintained at negative pressure relative to adjacent areas so air flows into the room rather than outward. It is the preferred inpatient placement for Airborne Precautions. Option A is correct. Positive-pressure rooms serve a different purpose, and ordinary private or semiprivate rooms do not provide equivalent engineering control.
source_row.source_detail: Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR): a single-occupancy room with monitored negative pressure relative to surrounding areas; AIIR placement is recommended for patients requiring Airborne Precautions. CDC isolation glossary current; live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
